name: 28-standing-desync-adopted
description:
A standing disagreement outside the readback-gate window - decided mode night, ISP rendering Day - is an external change (the operator's `color on`, a /control POST), first met on cam-wohn-ofen 2026-08-21 where it stood unreported for 90 s. It was first made visible (WARN, nothing enforced); the next step is that the automaton ADOPTS it once it has stood DN_DESYNC_MS (20 s, well past any switch transient, and the gate window already covers the 18 s after a commanded switch): cur takes the ISP's mode, nothing is switched or re-asserted, and the ordinary measurement judges it from there, as after a boot.

The shape: a stable lit interior at night (illuminator carries it, boot verify is silent, r=4). At t=60 the override forces the served ISP mode to Day; the day pipeline deliberately reads the SAME 2000 as the night pipeline so no trigger fires and the adopted day STANDS (a scene where a rule fires would test the rule, not the adoption). At t=150 the override is lifted: the ISP returns to the mode the board last commanded (night), which now disagrees with the adopted day and is adopted in turn. The budgets are the teeth: 2 board switches (the boot measurement's own pair) prove adoption drives nothing - a build that enforced or re-asserted would spend more - and the forbids on the gate's own lines prove the adoption did not fire THROUGH the gate.

expect_log: ISP has been rendering day for \d+ s while the decided mode was night - adopting the external change
ISP has been rendering night for \d+ s while the decided mode was day - adopting the external change
forbid_log: giving up until the next mode change
not enforcing, this may be a manual override
